result: In an uncontrolled cohort of 31 long COVID patients (~29 months ill), an 8-week Borg CR-10 pacing protocol cut PESE episodes by 15% per week (95% CI 11-20%) but did not clinically change overall LC symptoms.
reason: Same intervention, adds a long COVID pacing study; uncontrolled so does not alter the no-controlled-trial claim

result: In 534 ME/CFS patients with normal HR/BP on tilt vs 49 controls, 91% had abnormal CO and CBF reductions with a near 1:1 CO-CBF slope, CO largely predicting the CBF fall.
reason: Same Dutch clinic as van Campen 2020 (overlapping cohort), so not independent; adds CO-CBF mechanism

result: In 534 ME/CFS patients with normal HR/BP on tilt vs 49 controls, 91% had abnormal CO and CBF reductions with a near 1:1 CO-CBF slope.
reason: already cited (van Campen 2024 CO-CBF 1:1 result is in the finding detail)

result: FDG-PET in 87 PASC adults with neurocognitive symptoms found regional hypometabolism (pons -5.5%, right amygdala -4.2% vs controls; fusiform, amygdala, parahippocampal, vermis in 22-33% of patients) correlating with concentration and memory complaints.
reason: Same measure in long COVID; adds a positive series to the contested finding

result: FDG-PET in 87 PASC adults found the largest hypometabolism in the pons (-5.5% vs controls).
reason: Finding is ME/CFS structural/connectivity imaging; this is long COVID FDG metabolism, already linked to neuro-lc-fdg-pet

result: In a 9,820-member KPNC panel, 97.8% (95% CI 97.1-98.4%) of people with survey-defined ME/CFS-like illness had no ME/CFS diagnosis in the EHR; undiagnosed were younger and less often white non-Hispanic, and both groups were similarly impaired.
reason: Quantifies the under-diagnosis the finding notes for record-based prevalence; no prevalence rate given in abstract

result: In 30 long COVID vs 30 controls, RBC aggregation was higher and deformability higher but mechanical sensitivity limited (n=15 per group), with more morphological abnormalities that correlated with MS and FACIT-Fatigue.
reason: Different method and partly opposite deformability direction; small long COVID study adding morphology, not a replication

result: Serum spike was persistent in 11% of post-COVID healthy controls, 2% of PCS non-ME/CFS and 14% of post-COVID ME/CFS (121 PCS, 72 ME/CFS), with no association with severity, symptoms or labs; immunoadsorption reduced or removed spike in 5 patients.
reason: Supports post-COVID antigen persistence; null link to PCS matches the finding's modest-symptom-association caveat rather than contradicting the claim

result: In 100 tilt-verified post-COVID POTS patients vs 100 population controls, 24-h ambulatory BP showed higher nighttime and 24-h SBP, more nondipping (34% vs 19%) and more daytime hypotensive episodes.
reason: Objective autonomic/BP measurement in long COVID POTS, adds circadian BP dysregulation

result: In 100 post-COVID POTS patients vs 100 controls, ambulatory BP showed higher nighttime SBP and more nondipping (34% vs 19%).
reason: Does not measure POTS prevalence in ME/CFS; covered by neuro-lc-autonomic-objective link
